chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the owned slave, what is permissible for him from women? He said: Two free women, or four slave girls. He said: And there is no problem if his master permits him to buy from his wealth, if he has a slave girl or slave girls whom he may have relations with, and his slave girls are permissible for him.

key_terms.يَطَؤُهُنَّ: to have relations with them / to lie with them

ai.seo_question: What are the marital and sexual rights of a male slave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific marital rights of a male slave, distinguishing between his right to marry free women or own slave girls as distinct categories of permissible partners. It further establishes the legal mechanism for a slave to acquire concubines through his own wealth with the master's consent, reflecting the socio-economic realities of slavery in early Islamic society. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of 'raqiq' (slaves) as both property and potential spouses, contingent upon the master's authority.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Hassan Bin Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the owned slave, ‘What is Permissible for him from the women?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two free women, or four slave girls’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem if his master was to permit for him, so he buys from his wealth, if there was a slave girl for him, or slave girls he could go to, and his slave girls would be Permissible for him’.
